commonErrors: Reporting a class without the follow-up duration.
Mixing Engel and ILAE classes in one outcome measure.
name: Engel Epilepsy Surgery Outcome Classification

version.label: Engel classification (Engel et al. 1993), classes I–IV with subclasses
version.detail: Class I free of disabling seizures; II rare disabling seizures; III worthwhile improvement; IV no worthwhile improvement. The ILAE outcome classification (2001) is a different system and is not combined.

purpose: Classifies seizure outcome after epilepsy surgery.
intendedPopulation: Patients after epilepsy surgery, usually assessed at least 1–2 years after surgery.

calculatorNotice.title: State the follow-up period
calculatorNotice.message: Engel class depends on the period assessed. Report the follow-up duration with the class.

options.label: IA: Completely seizure free since surgery
IB: Non-disabling simple partial seizures only since surgery
IC: Some disabling seizures after surgery, but free of disabling seizures for at least 2 years
ID: Generalised convulsions with antiepileptic drug discontinuation only
IIA: Initially free of disabling seizures, but has rare seizures now
IIB: Rare disabling seizures since surgery
IIC: More than rare disabling seizures after surgery, but rare seizures for at least 2 years
IIIB: Prolonged seizure-free intervals amounting to more than half of the follow-up period, but not less than 2 years

resultStates.label: Class I: free of disabling seizures
resultStates.summary: Engel {cls_code}: free of disabling seizures at this assessment.
resultStates.detail: Outcome can change with longer follow-up; report the follow-up duration and medication status.

resultStates.label: Class II: rare disabling seizures
resultStates.summary: Engel {cls_code}: rare disabling seizures ('almost seizure free').

resultStates.label: Class IV: no worthwhile improvement
resultStates.detail: Assess seizure type, frequency and medication according to the clinical situation; the class does not by itself direct further treatment.

clinicalContext.text: The most widely reported seizure outcome classification after epilepsy surgery.
Terms such as 'disabling', 'rare' and 'worthwhile' are not defined numerically.

clinicalInsights.text: Report the follow-up duration and whether antiseizure medication has changed.
The ILAE classification uses seizure days relative to baseline and is assessed yearly; it can be reported alongside Engel.

limitations.text: Key terms ('disabling', 'rare', 'worthwhile') are subjective, which lowers agreement between centres.

limitations: Does not capture quality of life, cognition or medication burden.
Outcome can change with longer follow-up.

confounders.effect: Withdrawal can provoke seizures; continued medication can mask outcome.

whatItDoesNotTellYou: Quality of life or psychosocial outcome.
Cognitive or neurological side effects of surgery.

guideSections.what: Four outcome classes after epilepsy surgery (I–IV), each with subclasses.
guideSections.whenToUse: Reporting seizure outcome after resective or other epilepsy surgery.
guideSections.howToPerform: Review the seizure history since surgery, including seizure type, frequency, the most recent 2 years and medication changes. Choose the subclass that fits and record the follow-up duration.
guideSections.clinicalContext: An outcome classification; consider quality of life, cognition and medication alongside it.

sources.citation: Engel J Jr, Van Ness PC, Rasmussen TB, Ojemann LM. Outcome with respect to epileptic seizures. In: Engel J Jr, ed. Surgical Treatment of the Epilepsies. 2nd ed. New York: Raven Press; 1993:609-621.
